newsitem.title: UK: Windfall tax attacks will backfire, UK Labour says.
newsitem.headline: Windfall tax attacks will backfire, UK Labour says.

text.p: The opposition Labour party warned Britain's privatised utilties on Sunday not to campaign against Labour's planned windfall tax on their excess profits.

"As the election campaign goes on, the utilities will come to realise that it is counterproductive for them to spend huge sums of money and in the end alienate the public by standing up for a special and vested interest," economics spokesman Gordon Brown told BBC television's Breakfast with Frost programme.
He added: "I think those people who are trying to frighten... Labour supporters over the windfall tax by enormous and expensive publicity campaigns from the utilities are absolutely wrong."
Brown said he would announce the level of the tax, after consulting with industry regulators, in his first budget if Labour wins the coming general election, due by May 22.

There has been speculation that the windfall tax could raise five billion pounds, which Labour plans to spend on measures to reduce unemployment. Brown refused to be drawn, saying only that "it's going to raise substantial sums of money."
Brown dismissed suggestions that the tax could be struck down by the courts. "It is legally iron tight," he said.

"We are going ahead with this tax. It will be something that will yield resources for a purpose... and I think the public will see this as a fair tax which is justified because of the excess profits of the privatised utilities," Brown said.
